cfg_edges.rationale: The daily run retrieves the event records.
Days remaining are calculated for the filtered events.
The window filter keeps the 0–7 day events.
Each due event gets a generated reminder.
The second daily run retrieves the important days.
Each day is checked against the configured value.

cfg_edges.condition: days remaining equals the configured notify-days-before value
cfg_edges.rationale: Matching days are checked for duplicates.

cfg_edges.condition: no existing notification for the upcoming occurrence
cfg_edges.rationale: Non-duplicate days receive a generated reminder.
The webhook request feeds content generation.
The JSON is returned in the response.

dfg_edges.rationale: The schedule signal starts the retrieval.
Days are calculated for the filtered events.
The window filter consumes the computed days.
The loop iterates over the due events.
Generation uses the current event's details.
The send consumes the generated subject and body.
The log records the sent notification.
The log records the event context.
The schedule signal starts the important-days retrieval.
Occurrence calculation consumes the important days.
The match check consumes the computed occurrences.
Duplicate checking consumes the matching days.
The send consumes the generated subject and body.
Generation uses the platform, topic and audience inputs.
The response returns the stored content JSON.

notes: Three independent lanes share one system: (A) daily event reminders with a Supabase notifications log, (B) daily important-day reminders with duplicate prevention, and (C) webhook-driven content generation. Two native behaviors were excluded as undeclared implementation details and disclosed here: (1) the event-date resolution branch in lane (A) (preserve original date vs set next event date, then merge) — the frozen requirement declares only the 0–7 day window, which Gold models as a single window filter; (2) the pending 'Important Day' notification record written in lane (B) between the duplicate check and email generation — the frozen requirement declares only the duplicate check for lane (B), not a record write. Ordering note: the native computes days remaining inside the per-event loop, whereas Gold places the window filter before the loop; the two are behaviorally equivalent for the declared behavior. The webhook inputs are declared as platform/topic/audience; a source span additionally lists tone and length, which was noted but not elevated above the frozen requirement text. Failure handling is not specified in the frozen requirement.
